key_insight: Microscopic impurities seed degradation in perovskite films, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can rapidly flag this stability risk.
engineering_relevance: Rapid, non-invasive impurity screening could support quality control for scalable production of wide-bandgap perovskite films used in tandem solar cells.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation initiation sites.
Detect and quantify impurities within seconds using reflected-light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation initiating at impurity–perovskite interfaces, while films with higher impurity density exhibited faster early degradation.
watch_item: The abstract does not report detection accuracy or validation across different fabrication processes, leaving deployment robustness uncertain.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
